neighbours.label: references to science-fiction films and fictional AIs in discussions of AI: the token right after a named work (Her [and] Ex Machina, HAL 9000 [or] Skynet)
fire: Films such as Her and Ex Machina explore what it means for a machine to love.
We are still far from HAL 9000 or Skynet, despite the hype about chatbots.
Movies like The Terminator, Blade Runner and The Matrix shaped public fears of AI.
Fiction from Asimov's robot stories to Westworld imagines machines that rebel.
Critics compared the chatbot to the computer in 2001: A Space Odyssey and to Data from Star Trek.
The debate about robot rights echoes the movie A.I. and the novel Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep.
Many engineers first got interested in AI after watching WarGames or Short Circuit.
Iain Banks's Culture novels imagine benevolent machine minds running a galaxy.
quiet: Researchers are exploring what it means for a machine to learn from feedback.
We are still far from general intelligence, despite the hype about chatbots.
News reports about job losses shaped public fears of AI.
Studies from economists to sociologists examine how machines change work.
Critics compared the chatbot to earlier software and to search engines.
The debate about robot rights echoes older arguments about animal welfare.
Many engineers first got interested in AI after taking a statistics course.
Some philosophers imagine benevolent machine minds running a future economy.
